workstations.name: River & weather
workstations.description: Track the river, forecast, and exposed routes.

workstations.name: Field operations
workstations.description: Coordinate field reports, crews, and critical services.

roles.name: Communications & command
roles.focus: Track field reports, weigh conflicting accounts, and coordinate the response.

roles.name: Earth systems analyst
roles.focus: Read the river gauges and rainfall forecast. Connect conditions upstream to risk downstream.

roles.name: Geography analyst
roles.focus: Compare elevation, exposed communities, and the routes that can still carry people out.

roles.name: Operations officer
roles.focus: Match available crews to routes, shelters, and critical infrastructure.

locations.name: Pine Valley
locations.detail: Low-lying homes beside the river. The east ridge road is the only route above the projected flood line.

locations.name: North bridge
locations.detail: A vital river crossing. Water is approaching the deck; structural condition needs field verification.

locations.name: Old harbor
locations.detail: Waterfront streets and businesses. Low ground is exposed to river overflow and the afternoon high tide.

locations.name: Bay hospital
locations.detail: 180 patients. Backup power is ready, but fuel arrives by the lower river road.

locations.name: Ridge shelter
locations.detail: Space for 900 residents. Access is via the east ridge road, safely above the modeled flood area.

locations.name: Upstream gauge
locations.detail: Automatic river-level station. Reports every five simulated minutes; debris may affect the sensor.

evidence.title: Water reaches the lower river road
evidence.body: A responder has confirmed standing water across the lower river road. Vehicles can still use the east ridge road. Residents in Pine Valley have not yet received an evacuation instruction.

evidence.title: River rising 0.4 m per hour
evidence.body: The river gauge reads 4.2 m, up from 3.8 m one hour ago. The local flood threshold is 4.8 m. At the current rate it would be reached in about 90 minutes, but upstream rainfall could accelerate the rise.

evidence.title: One route stays above the flood line
evidence.body: The lower river road lies at 5–7 m elevation. The east ridge road climbs to 32 m and reaches Ridge shelter at 64 m. North bridge lies on the lower route and may become impassable.

evidence.title: Eight crews; shelter capacity is limited
evidence.body: Eight response crews are available for this operation. Ridge shelter can receive 900 people; Pine Valley has 1,240 residents. Additional evacuees will need onward transport. Crews committed to a task remain assigned for the rest of this exercise.

evidence.title: Social posts claim the bridge has failed
evidence.body: A widely shared post says North bridge has collapsed. There is no timestamped image or responder confirmation. The latest camera still shows the deck standing. Treat the structure's condition as unknown until a field assessment arrives.

evidence.title: Heavy rain stalls over the headwaters
evidence.body: Radar indicates a slow-moving rain band over the upper watershed. Another 25–40 mm is possible over the next hour. This is a forecast range, not an observed total; river rise may accelerate.

evidence.title: Bridge standing; approach is unsafe
evidence.body: Inspectors confirm the bridge deck is intact. Debris is collecting at the piers and floodwater covers the western approach. The collapse rumor was inaccurate, but civilian traffic should be diverted.

evidence.title: Hospital fuel delivery interrupted
evidence.body: The scheduled generator-fuel delivery cannot use the lower river road. The hospital has 180 patients. A logistics crew can move reserve fuel by the ridge route before surface access becomes slower.

evidence.title: Flood threshold exceeded
evidence.body: Water has reached 5.1 m, exceeding the 4.8 m flood threshold. The river is now spilling into the low-lying floodplain. Earlier forecasts underestimated the speed of the rise.

evidence.title: Harbor streets filling with water
evidence.body: Water is entering ground-floor businesses at Old harbor. Responders need boats to move isolated residents to higher ground. Road vehicles cannot safely enter the waterfront.

evidence.title: Rain band moving east; rivers still high
evidence.body: The heaviest rain is moving away from the headwaters. Water levels remain high and could rise again if debris clears upstream. Keep routes restricted until a field team verifies them.

evidence.title: Pine Valley convoy is using the ridge road
evidence.body: The earlier evacuation order put transport crews on the ridge route before the low road flooded. Residents are moving toward high ground. The intake team is checking shelter capacity and arranging onward transport for people beyond the 900-space limit.

evidence.title: Pine Valley is still awaiting transport
evidence.body: No evacuation order was dispatched before the lower road flooded. The routine road-evacuation window has closed. Residents have been advised to stay on high ground while responders assess specialist rescue access.

actions.title: Move Pine Valley to higher ground
actions.description: Send transport crews along the east ridge road and move residents out before the lower route floods.
actions.tradeoff: Commits three crews. Ridge shelter holds 900 people; the remaining 340 need onward transport.
actions.outcome: Transport crews are moving toward Pine Valley via the ridge road. Evacuation and onward transport are being coordinated.

actions.title: Close and inspect North bridge
actions.description: Set up a diversion and send an inspection team to the flooded approach.
actions.tradeoff: Protects traffic at the crossing, but increases travel time to the hospital and harbor.
actions.outcome: North bridge is closed to civilian traffic. Responders have established a diversion via the east ridge road.

actions.title: Activate Ridge shelter
actions.description: Prepare shelter spaces, supplies, and an intake team on high ground.
actions.tradeoff: Two crews remain at the shelter. Opening the shelter alone does not move residents there.
actions.outcome: Shelter crews are preparing intake and supplies for up to 900 people at Ridge shelter.

actions.title: Secure hospital backup power
actions.description: Move reserve generator fuel to Bay hospital using the ridge route.
actions.tradeoff: Reserves one logistics crew that could otherwise support evacuation or shelter setup.
actions.outcome: A logistics crew is moving reserve fuel along the ridge route to support Bay hospital's essential systems.

actions.title: Deploy rescue boats to the harbor
actions.description: Send two specialist crews to help residents isolated by floodwater.
actions.tradeoff: Commits both boat crews. They cannot simultaneously support Pine Valley.
actions.outcome: Boat crews are transferring isolated harbor residents to higher ground.

bulletins.title: River rising. Communities on watch.
bulletins.summary: Floodwater has reached the lower river road. Pine Valley remains accessible by the east ridge route.
bulletins.forecast: Pine Valley could flood within 60–90 minutes if the river keeps rising. The ridge road is the strongest evacuation route in the current terrain model.
bulletins.uncertainty: Moderate confidence. Fresh upstream rainfall and a bridge assessment would narrow the estimate.

bulletins.title: Storm stalls over the upper watershed.
bulletins.summary: Another 25–40 mm of rain is forecast. North bridge is standing, but its western approach is unsafe.
bulletins.forecast: The stalled rain band increases the likelihood of river overflow. The evacuation window is narrowing; deploy before the next update to use the road route.
bulletins.uncertainty: Moderate confidence. Rainfall totals are a range. The bridge inspection has resolved the collapse rumor.

bulletins.title: Flood threshold crossed. Harbor cut off.
bulletins.summary: The gauge reads 5.1 m. Water is entering Old harbor; boat crews are needed on the waterfront.
bulletins.forecast: Low roads are now outside the safe operating envelope. Earlier evacuation orders reduce exposure; new waterfront rescues require boats.
bulletins.uncertainty: High confidence in observed flooding. The time of the peak remains uncertain.

bulletins.title: Rain easing. Response operations continue.
bulletins.summary: The rain band is moving east. High water and debris still make low roads unsafe.
bulletins.forecast: Rainfall is easing, but the floodplain will drain slowly. Maintain shelter, hospital support, and restricted routes while field teams reassess.
bulletins.uncertainty: Moderate confidence. An upstream debris release could cause another pulse of water.
